title: Piston Engine Operations & Engine Classification
subtitle: The four-stroke cycle is the fundamental operating sequence of most automobile engines. This week explains each stroke in detail, followed by a comprehensive classification of engines by fuel type, cylinder number, arrangement, operating cycle, and ignition type.
learningOutcome: The four-stroke cycle is the fundamental operating sequence of most automobile engines. This week explains each stroke in detail, followed by a comprehensive classification of engines by fuel type, cylinder number, arrangement, operating cycle, and ignition type.

content.text: A four-stroke engine is like a pump that goes through 4 steps to make power. Breathe in (intake) → squeeze (compression) → explode (power) → blow out (exhaust). The piston goes up and down twice (two complete up-down cycles = four strokes) to complete one full power cycle.

A four-stroke engine must undergo four different strokes to complete one cycle to produce power. The four strokes are: Intake, Compression, Power, Exhaust. Intake Stroke: The cam motion triggers the opening of the inlet valve creating a suction; hence the air-fuel mixture is entered the cylinder giving room for the second stroke as the inlet valve closes. Compression Stroke: Both the inlet valve and the compression valve remain closed. The air-fuel is further compressed to build up more pressure within the cylinder. At the end of this stroke, compressed air-fuel is ignited by the spark plug. Power Stroke: The explosion exerts pressure and pushes the piston down, giving power to the crank. Exhaust Stroke: The outlet valve opens and pushes out the burnt gas. This marks the end of a cycle and the whole process is repeated over and over again keeping the engine running and producing power.

items: With the aid of a diagram, describe the four strokes of a four-stroke internal combustion engine.
Distinguish between Spark Ignition (SI) and Compression Ignition (CI) engines.
Classify engines based on cylinder arrangement. What are the advantages of a V-engine over an inline engine?
What is the difference between a naturally aspirated engine and a turbocharged engine?

content.text: 1. Based on Fuel Type: — Internal Combustion Engines (ICE): Petrol Engines (use gasoline and spark ignition); Diesel Engines (use diesel fuel and compression ignition); Alternative Fuel Engines (CNG, LPG, other fuels). — Electric Motors: Electric vehicles (EVs) use batteries to power electric motors. — Hybrid Engines: Combine an ICE with an electric motor. Mild Hybrid (MHEV), Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV), Plug-in Hybrid (PHEV). 2. Based on Number of Cylinders: Single-cylinder (motorcycles); Twin-cylinder; Three-cylinder (fuel-efficient cars); Four-cylinder (most common); Six-cylinder; Eight-cylinder (V8); Ten-cylinder (V10); Twelve-cylinder (V12) (high-performance and luxury). 3. Based on Cylinder Arrangement: — Straight/Inline: Cylinders in a single line. — V-engine: Cylinders in two banks forming a "V" shape. — Flat or Boxer Engine: Cylinders arranged horizontally opposite each other. — W-engine: Combines two V-engines, creating a "W" shape. 4. Based on Operating Cycle: — Two-stroke engine: Completes the combustion cycle in two strokes of the piston. — Four-stroke engine: Completes the combustion cycle in four strokes of the piston. 5. Based on Ignition Type: — Spark Ignition (SI) engine: Uses a spark plug to ignite the air-fuel mixture (gasoline engines). — Compression Ignition (CI) engine: Compresses the air-fuel mixture to a high temperature, causing it to ignite (diesel engines). 6. Other Classifications: — Naturally Aspirated: Relies on atmospheric pressure to fill the cylinders. — Turbocharged: Uses an exhaust-driven turbine to force more air into the cylinders. — Supercharged: Uses a mechanical compressor to force more air in. — Air-cooled vs. Water-cooled: Refers to the method of cooling the engine.

Common mistake — Students confuse SI and CI engines by saying "diesel engines use spark plugs." Wrong — diesel (CI) engines do NOT have spark plugs. They ignite fuel by compressing air to such a high temperature that injected diesel spontaneously combusts. Spark plugs are only in petrol (SI) engines.
